title: Special Act on the Establishment and Operation of Urban-Type Campuses
full_text:
SPECIAL ACT ON THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF URBAN-TYPE CAMPUSES

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to contribute to improving the educational environment by increasing the flexibility and diversity of the operation of schools and school facilities through prescribing matters necessary for the smooth establishment and operation of urban-type campuses.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on March 5, 2026>
1. "Public school" means a public school under Article 3 (2) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
2. "Urban-type campus" means a branch school of a public school established to respond appropriately to changes in commuting conditions and the school-age population in a Special Metropolitan City, Integrated Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, or an urban area with a population of at least 200,000 other than such cities, under the Local Autonomy Act.
3. "Main school" means the public school that operates and manages an urban-type campus.
4. "Branch school" means a school that, in school facilities separate from those of the main school and under the direction and supervision of the head of the main school, provides some or all of the education provided by the main school.

Article 3 (Relationship with Other Acts) With respect to matters concerning the establishment and operation of urban-type campuses as prescribed by this Act, this Act shall prevail over other Acts, including the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.

CHAPTER II ESTABLISHMENT OF URBAN-TYPE CAMPUSES

Article 4 (Establishment of Urban-Type Campuses)
(1) Where necessary to alleviate long-distance commutes or overcrowded classes, the Superintendent of Education of a Special Metropolitan City, Integrated Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Province (hereinafter referred to as a "Si/Do") (hereinafter referred to as the "Superintendent of Education") may establish an urban-type campus within the relevant city. <Amended on March 5, 2026>
(2) The Superintendent of Education may prescribe standards for establishing urban-type campuses by ordinance of the relevant Si/Do, taking into consideration local conditions and student placement plans.
(3) The Superintendent of Education may prescribe standards for school buildings (meaning facilities directly or indirectly necessary for teaching and learning activities, including classrooms and libraries) and playgrounds of urban-type campuses by ordinance of the relevant Si/Do.

Article 5 (Names)
(1) An urban-type campus shall indicate the name of the main school before the name of the urban-type campus.
(2) Other matters necessary concerning the names of urban-type campuses shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Education.

Article 6 (Types and Categories)
(1) The types and categories of urban-type campuses shall be as follows:
1. Reorganized urban-type campus: An urban-type campus formed by reorganizing an existing school that has become small due to a decrease in the school-age population;
2. Newly established urban-type campus: An urban-type campus newly established to alleviate overcrowding resulting from an influx of the school-age population into a particular area, meet school demand arising from urban development projects, address long-distance commutes, or improve commuting conditions.
(2) Other detailed matters concerning the types and categories of urban-type campuses shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Education.

CHAPTER III OPERATION OF URBAN-TYPE CAMPUSES

Article 7 (Curricula)
(1) The curriculum of an urban-type campus shall be the same as that of its main school.
(2) Where necessary in consideration of regional characteristics and student composition, the Superintendent of Education may operate curricula by separating students of the main school and urban-type campus according to grade or department.

Article 8 (Student Self-Government Activities) Basic matters concerning the organization and operation of student self-government activities at an urban-type campus shall be prescribed by school regulations. In such cases, the opinions of students of the main school and the urban-type campus shall be collected regarding whether student self-governing organizations are to be operated jointly or separately.

Article 9 (School Personnel)
(1) The head of an urban-type campus shall be the head of its main school, and separate staffing quotas shall be established for the faculty and staff of the urban-type campus other than the head, distinct from those of the main school.
(2) The Superintendent of Education may assign faculty and staff in consideration of the characteristics of an urban-type campus and may permit faculty and staff of the main school to hold concurrent duties insofar as this does not impede school operations.
(3) Other matters concerning staffing quotas and assignments of faculty and staff of urban-type campuses shall be governed by the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.

Article 10 (School Operating Committees)
(1) A school operating committee established for an urban-type campus shall be operated jointly with the main school. In such cases, at least one member of the main school's school operating committee shall be a parent or teacher of the urban-type campus.
(2) Where necessary for efficient management, the head of the main school may establish and operate a separate school operating committee for the urban-type campus.
(3) Other matters concerning the composition and operation of school operating committees shall be governed by the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.

Article 11 (School Meals)
(1) Where necessary to provide school meals at an urban-type campus, the head of the main school shall separately manage and operate the relevant facilities, equipment, and personnel.
(2) Other matters necessary for school meals at urban-type campuses shall be governed by the School Meals Act.

Article 12 (Integrated or Separate School Operation)
(1) School accounts, public property, and goods of an urban-type campus shall be operated in an integrated manner with those of the main school.
(2) Where necessary for the efficient operation of an urban-type campus, the Superintendent of Education may operate facilities, equipment, and similar assets separately from the main school.

ADDENDUM <No. 20665, January 21, 2025>
Article 1 (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force one year after the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Transitional Measures) Branch schools of public schools established and operated before the enforcement of this Act in Special Metropolitan Cities, Metropolitan Cities, Special Self-Governing Cities, and urban areas with a population of at least 200,000 other than such cities under the Local Autonomy Act shall be deemed urban-type campuses established under this Act.

ADDENDUM (Local Autonomy Act) <No. 21447, March 5, 2026>
Article 1 (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force on July 1, 2026: Provided, That amendments under Article 2 of these Addenda to Acts promulgated before this Act enters into force but not yet effective shall enter into force on the respective effective dates of those Acts.

Article 2 (Amendment of Other Acts) (1) through (11) Omitted.

(12) Part of the Special Act on the Establishment and Operation of Urban-Type Campuses shall be amended as follows:

In subparagraph 2 of Article 2, "Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, and cities with a population of at least 200,000 other than Special Metropolitan Cities, Metropolitan Cities, and Special Self-Governing Cities" shall be replaced with "Special Metropolitan City, Integrated Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, and cities with a population of at least 200,000 other than Special Metropolitan Cities, Integrated Special Metropolitan Cities, Metropolitan Cities, and Special Self-Governing Cities".

In Article 4 (1), "Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, and Do" shall be replaced with "Special Metropolitan City, Integrated Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, and Do".

(13) through (32) Omitted.
